# SessionMutationAfterClose

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Detect a write to $_SESSION after successful session_write_close and before a proven session_start reopening.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
session_start(); session_write_close(); $_SESSION['visits']++;
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Persist session changes before closing the session.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report a write to $_SESSION after successful session_write_close and before a proven session_start reopening.
- Resolve builtin calls and named arguments before checking the contract. Project-local callees are considered only when their bodies or immutable summaries establish the required facts. The default is enabled, with positive proof required.
- For flow-dependent conditions, require a reachable source-to-use path with no intervening invalidation. Unknown calls, ambiguous aliases, recursion or analysis-budget exhaustion cannot establish definite facts.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Reads, reopened sessions, failed close, externally persisted session wrappers and unknown session state are excluded.
- Unresolved targets, incomplete required facts, suppressed findings and PHP versions lacking the referenced API or language feature produce no report. User declarations shadowing builtin names are not builtin contracts.
- Assigning an empty array to the whole `$_SESSION` (`$_SESSION = [];`, `$_SESSION = array();`) clears the in-memory copy of a closed session; no change is meant to persist. Writes of a key, compound assignments and non-empty arrays stay reported.

## Fix

No automatic fix: moving writes or reopening a session changes locking and failure behavior.

## PHP versions

Apply only on PHP versions supporting the referenced APIs and syntax (within PHP 5.3–8.5). Builtin behavior and argument contracts follow the configured PHP version. Extension-specific calls require resolved extension API symbols; do not treat same-named application functions as extension calls.

## Options

None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "SessionMutationAfterClose": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore SessionMutationAfterClose
```
